NPU03624 is a specific laboratory test code used within the Danish healthcare system to identify the measurement of thyrotropin, commonly known as thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) [^src1]. In the context of the national clinical quality indicators for atrial fibrillation (the AFDK program), NPU03624 is officially recognized as one of the valid codes that count toward the fulfillment of indicator 3, which tracks whether patients have received a TSH measurement [^src1]. 

The code appears in the technical documentation published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), which provides the precise definitions, denominators, numerators, and exclusion criteria for monitoring the quality of atrial fibrillation treatment [^src1]. In the 2024 guidelines, NPU03624 is listed among a specific set of laboratory and procedure codes (including NPU27547 and NPU04199) used to capture TSH testing in health registries [^src1]. By the 2025 update of the AFDK report, the registry code lists were expanded to include additional identifiers (such as AS000646 and RSD03382), but NPU03624 remained a constant, foundational code for tracking this specific biomarker, [[thyreoideastimulerende-hormon-tsh|thyreoideastimulerende hormon (TSH)]] [^src2].
